_meta.indication: TIVICAY is an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) indicated in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and children aged 12 years and older and weighing at least 40 kg.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, international, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled; DTG 50 mg once daily vs RAL 400 mg twice daily, each with 2 NRTIs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48 (Snapshot)
pivotal_trials.result: DTG non-inferior to RAL: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL 88% vs 86% (treatment difference 2.6%, 95% CI -1.9%, 7.2%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind; DTG 50 mg once daily + ABC/LAM (EPZICOM) vs ATRIPLA (efavirenz/FTC/TDF)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48 (Snapshot)
pivotal_trials.result: DTG superior to ATRIPLA: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL 88% vs 81% (treatment difference 7.4%, 95% CI 2.5%, 12.3%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized; DTG 50 mg once daily vs RAL 400 mg twice daily with investigator-selected background regimen (up to 2 agents, >=1 fully active)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion with HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 24 (Snapshot)
pivotal_trials.result: DTG superior to RAL: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL 79% vs 70% (adjusted treatment difference 9.7%, 95% CI 3.4%, 15.9%)

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of GSK1349572 Versus Raltegravir (RAL) With Investigator Selected Background Regimen in Antiretroviral-Experienced, Integrase Inhibitor-Naive Adults

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions of moderate to severe intensity and incidence >=2% were insomnia and headache. Safety concerns leading to discontinuation included hypersensitivity reactions, hepatic enzyme elevations (predominantly in hepatitis B and C infected patients), and development of renal insufficiency or renal failure.
target_moa: Dolutegravir inhibits HIV integrase by binding to the integrase active site and blocking the strand transfer step of retroviral DNA integration, essential for the HIV replication cycle.
modality: small molecule new molecular entity (integrase strand transfer inhibitor)

advisory_committee.vote: This NDA was not presented before the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee; no issues required outside expertise.

description.text: Expanded indication to include dolutegravir in combination with rilpivirine as a complete regimen to replace current antiretroviral regimen in virologically suppressed patients

citations.quote: - To expand the indication to include the use of TIVICAY (dolutegravir) in combination with rilpivirine as a complete regimen to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen for at least 6 months with no history of treatment failure or known substitutions associated with resistance to either antiretroviral.

basis.text: Granted priority review because DTG provides significant improvement in the treatment of HIV-infected adults and children, including treatment-experienced adults who have failed an INSTI-containing regimen, and is dosed once daily.

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review because DTG provides a significant improvement in the treatment of HIV-infected adults and children including treatment-experienced adults who have failed an INSTI-containing antiretroviral regimen.

summary.text: Standard (non-accelerated) full approval of a small-molecule INSTI received December 17, 2012 and granted priority review; the NDA was not taken to advisory committee as it was the third INSTI in class.

citations.quote: The NDA for DTG was submitted and received on December 17, 2012, and reviewed under the PDUFA V program.

The application was granted a priority review because DTG provides a significant improvement in the treatment of HIV-infected adults and children including treatment-experienced adults who have failed an INSTI-containing antiretroviral regimen.
This NDA was not presented before the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee. It was the third INSTI in the class. Notably, no issues were identified that required outside expertise.
